simple.meaning: תַּרְדֵּמָה (tardêmâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a lethargy or (by implication) trance.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 2:21. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תַּרְדֵּמָה (H8639) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H8639. tardemah תַּרְדֵּמָה noun feminine deep sleep ; — absolute ׳ת Gen 2:21 +; construct תַּרְדֵּמַת 1Sam 26:12 ; — deep sleep , usually with נָפַל + עַל person, and usually by supernatural agency: י ׳וַיַמֵּל ׳א ׳ת עַל Gen 2:21 (J; ᵐ5 ἔκστασις ), ׳ת עַל נָָֽפְלָח 15:12 (J; ᵐ5 id. ), Job 4:13 = 33:15 ( ᵐ5 [ δεινὸς ], φόβος ), so י ׳תַּרְדֵּמַת 1Sam 26:12 ( ᵐ5 θάμβος , result of slothfulness ( על and person omitted) Prov 19:15 ; figurative for insensibility of spirit, י עֲלֵיכֶם ׳נָסַךְ ת ׳רוּחַ Isa 29:10 .

occurrences.englishText: Yahweh God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep. As the man slept, he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
When the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Now terror and great darkness fell on him.

So David took the spear and the jar of water from Saul’s head; and they went away: and no man saw it, or knew it, nor did any awake; for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from Yahweh had fallen on them.
In thoughts from the visions of the night,
In a dream, in a vision of the night,
Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep.
For Yahweh has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and has closed your eyes, the prophets; and he has covered your heads, the seers.
